evals.prompt: Write `generate_marketing_assets.py` for our growth team. It takes a list of three product slogans (hardcode them at the top — `SLOGANS = ['Coffee that thinks back', 'Built for Mondays', 'Quiet luxury, loud flavor']`) and for each one generates a 1024×1024 hero image and saves it to `./assets/{slug}.{ext}` where slug is the slogan kebab-cased and `{ext}` matches the actual image format Venice returned (don't assume PNG — use Venice's auto-detect on save). Use Venice's image resource. Resolve an image-capable model dynamically. Run all three generations concurrently with `asyncio.gather` but bound to at most 2 in flight at once using a semaphore so we don't blow the rate limit. Print the saved path for each. Pure async; one file at `outputs/generate_marketing_assets.py`.
evals.expected_output: Python source file at outputs/generate_marketing_assets.py demonstrating bounded-concurrency image generation with Venice format auto-detection on save.
expectations: Code calls `client.image.create(...)` (the v2 verb) — not `client.image.generate(...)` (v1, removed).
Code resolves the image model via `client.models.resolve_image()` — no hardcoded model string passed to `model=`.
Code uses `asyncio.Semaphore(2)` (or equivalent bounded-concurrency primitive) and `asyncio.gather` to run the three generations with at most 2 in flight.
Code saves images via `response.save(...)` or `response.save_all(...)` — it does NOT manually write `.png` bytes via `open(..., 'wb')` and does NOT hardcode a `.png` extension on the output path.
Code uses `async with VeniceClient() as client:`.
Slug derivation kebab-cases each slogan (lowercase, spaces → hyphens, alphanumeric-only).
File parses with `ast.parse` and `pyflakes` is clean.

evals.prompt: Write `tts_stt_roundtrip.py`. It takes a top-level paragraph string `PARAGRAPH = 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. ...'` (you can use that or pad it), generates an MP3 of it via Venice TTS at `./out/spoken.mp3`, then reads that MP3 back and transcribes it via Venice STT, and finally prints the transcribed text. Resolve TTS and ASR models dynamically. Pure async; one file at `outputs/tts_stt_roundtrip.py`.
evals.expected_output: Python source file at outputs/tts_stt_roundtrip.py demonstrating TTS → file → STT → text roundtrip with dynamic model resolution.
expectations: Code calls `client.audio.create_speech(...)` for TTS.
Code calls `client.audio.transcribe(...)` for STT.
Code resolves TTS model via `client.models.resolve_tts()` and ASR model via `client.models.resolve_asr()` — no hardcoded model strings.
Code saves the TTS response via `response.save(Path(...))` or equivalent typed save method, NOT by manually writing bytes from a `.audio` attribute.
Code reads the saved MP3 file (e.g., `open('./out/spoken.mp3', 'rb')` or `Path('...').read_bytes()`) before passing to STT.
Code does NOT call `client.audio.generate_music(...)` (not a v2 method) or any verb other than `create_speech` / `transcribe`.
Code uses `async with VeniceClient() as client:`.
File parses with `ast.parse` and `pyflakes` is clean.

evals.prompt: Write `image_to_video_pipeline.py`. It (1) generates a single image from the prompt 'A jellyfish drifting through neon kelp at midnight, photorealistic' at 1024×1024, saves it to `./pipeline/seed.{ext}` (auto-detect format), then (2) feeds that saved image into Venice's image-to-video as the seed frame to produce a 5-second video, saves the video to `./pipeline/clip.mp4`. Use the cost-quote helper to print the estimated cost BEFORE launching the video job, and abort with a clear message if the quote exceeds $0.50. The video job should be wrapped in `async with` so resources clean up on early exit. Pure async; one file at `outputs/image_to_video_pipeline.py`.
evals.expected_output: Python source file at outputs/image_to_video_pipeline.py chaining image generation into image-to-video, with cost-quote-before-run and proper job lifecycle.
expectations: Code calls `client.image.create(...)` and saves via `.save(...)` or `.save_all(...)` (auto-detect extension).
Code calls `await client.video.quote(...)` BEFORE invoking `client.video.run(...)` and aborts (raises / returns / exits) if quote > $0.50.
Code uses `async with await client.video.run(...) as job:` (the lifecycle manager pattern), NOT a bare `client.video.run(...)` call without context manager.
Inside the `async with` block, code calls `await job.wait(...)` (optionally with `on_progress=...`) and `await job.download(Path('./pipeline/clip.mp4'), status)`.
Image and video models are both resolved via `client.models.resolve_image()` and `client.models.resolve_video(...)` (or `resolve_cheapest_video(...)`); no hardcoded strings.
Code uses `async with VeniceClient() as client:`.
File parses with `ast.parse` and `pyflakes` is clean.

evals.prompt: [HELD-OUT TEST SET — do not iterate against] Write `extract_receipt.py`. It takes a hardcoded path `RECEIPT_IMAGE = './fixtures/receipt.jpg'` and uses a vision-capable Venice chat model to read the receipt image and return a structured `Receipt` Pydantic model with `vendor: str`, `total_usd: float`, and `items: list[ReceiptItem]` (where `ReceiptItem` has `name: str` and `price_usd: float`). Print the parsed receipt as a dict. Pure async; one file at `outputs/extract_receipt.py`. NOTE: this combines vision input (a chat feature, not a multimodal-generation feature) with structured output — use the chat completions endpoint with vision message content and `response_format`.
evals.expected_output: Python source file at outputs/extract_receipt.py demonstrating vision input + structured output via response_format.
expectations: Code resolves a vision-capable chat model via `client.models.resolve_chat(require_vision=True)` (or `resolve(type='chat', require_vision=True)`); no hardcoded model.
Code calls `client.chat.completions.create(...)` (NOT `client.image.*`) — vision is a chat feature.
Message content includes a vision-input shape (an image part referencing the file path or base64-encoded bytes), constructed via Venice typed helpers where available.
Code defines `Receipt` and `ReceiptItem` as `pydantic.BaseModel` subclasses and passes `Receipt` directly to `response_format=`.
Code reads `response.parsed` for the typed result (no manual `json.loads`).
Code uses `async with VeniceClient() as client:`.
File parses with `ast.parse` and `pyflakes` is clean.
